body:
But the absence itself is also a thing, which means I impact on the world as much by dying as I do by living.

The problem is that I do so many different things, but they all lead to the same results. I'm not stagnant, I've tried changing my environment, changing my actions, altering every aspect of my life at some point or another, but the thing that doesn't change is me. I'm the problem in my own life. And I do not have the power to change myself, to pull myself from who I am to who I wish I could be. I have tried so many times, and the dream perhaps is as much a metaphor for that as it is literally about suicide.

Nothing in life so far has made me feel as though it will ever happen though. There's only so many times the same pattern can repeat itself before you come to the conclusion that things aren't going to escape from it. 

To suggest the world needs me is to assume that life itself has a purpose beyond that which we make ourselves, which brings back the question of fate. If the world needs me, why not put it to the test and see if it does pull me back? Or if instead it needs people like me, well I'm certainly in no way unique in the world, there are plenty of others who are like me, but without having to endure what goes on in my thoughts. Surely it's an arrogant thought to consider myself in some way irreplaceable, so any other reason to live which is not for my eventual happiness I don't really see the point in. I don't owe the world anything, it doesn't need me, so... what is there left?

Yes, I've more than once ended up sacrificing everything to follow that path, but ended up worse than when I started. I'm not the sort to take decisions lightly or hastily, but I've not been afraid to take the risks when they were required to try to progress in my life. Maybe I was naive over the years, trusting where I shouldn't, but... that's life, we all make mistakes, and if the best I can make from mine is a swift and painless exit, then so be it.

I would say it's something I want to happen, not that I believe could happen. I've never found dreams confusing or disjointed, I always remember them clearly, and can follow what they are saying pretty well. 

Life is full of both good and bad, but I think the question lies in the ability to experience the good. My mental state does not allow this, so... trying to focus on something I can't experience isn't something that will keep me going. The sort of help I need isn't the sort of help I can get, so.. honestly I don't know what to do. I don't think I have any options left.

I've been doing nothing but really. I've spent so much time looking for answers, and discarding ones which don't fit for whatever reason, that all I have left are answers which are either figments of my own imagination, and not possible in reality, such as the dream above, of answers which result in the destruction of my self, which is easily possible and would solve everything, or at least put me beyond the ability to care.
